> 大過。棟橈。利有攸往，亨。

Hexagram 28 is the one whose picture is literally its shape, and that is where to start.

## 棟橈: a ridgepole bending

棟 is the main beam at the ridge of a roof. 橈: 說文 曲木也 — bent wood, bowing downward.

And here the form has to be looked at: 大過's six lines are 初六 and 上六 at the two ends, with four solid lines in between.

Two ends empty; the middle packed.

The 彖 says it in three characters: 本末弱也 — the root is weak, the tip is weak.

So the hexagram's image is a cross-section of a bent beam. The weight is all in the middle and there is nothing at either end to hold it. Which is not a moral statement; it is a structural one, and the rest of the chapter works outward from it.

## 過 is to exceed the measure

過's original sense is to pass through; the extension is to surpass, to go beyond the constant measure.

大過: the great has exceeded the mean.

Which is a condition, not a crime. The chapter's advice is not "return to the mean" — with four solid lines in the middle, that is not available. The advice is what to do while the beam is bending.

## 藉用白茅

初六 藉用白茅，無咎.

藉: to spread a mat. White cogongrass under the offering.

The plainest possible material, laid with the most care.

And this is the correct posture at the very beginning of an excessive time: nothing elaborate, everything placed carefully. 無咎 without a 吉 — the line does not promise success, only that nothing is damaged.

## 枯楊生稊 / 枯楊生華

九二: 枯楊生稊 — the withered willow puts out a new shoot from the root. 老夫得其女妻，無不利.

九五: 枯楊生華 — the withered willow flowers. 老婦得其士夫，無咎無譽.

稊 is a shoot from the base: the renewal comes from inside, from the root.
華 is a flower: it opens outward, shows, and falls.

So the pair is the hexagram's central discrimination — renewal that grows from the root versus display that blooms on dead wood. One is 無不利; the other is 無咎無譽, neither blamed nor praised.

And the images are attached to May-December marriages in both cases: the same kind of arrangement, once with a shoot and once with a flower.

## 棟隆 / 棟橈

九三 棟橈，凶.
九四 棟隆，吉；有它吝.

隆 is raised, sound. So: the beam bends (3), and the beam holds (4).

Same structural condition, adjacent lines, opposite verdicts — because line 3 is firm in a firm place and pushes past what the beam can take, while line 4 is firm in a yielding place and lets the load be distributed.

So 大過's difference between collapse and survival is not strength. It is the willingness to be in a soft position while carrying a hard load.

## 過涉滅頂，凶，無咎

Top line: crossing the water, the water goes over the head. 凶, and 無咎.

Two verdicts on one act: it failed, and no one is at fault.

Which is the book's most exact statement about the limits of a time like this. The person did the right thing and drowned. 凶 is the outcome; 無咎 is the accounting. Keeping both is the whole difficulty of reading 大過 honestly.

## 獨立不懼，遯世無悶

The 象: stand alone without fear; withdraw from the world without stifling.

Which is a strange instruction for a chapter about a collapsing roof. It does not say "save the roof." It says: in a time when the structure is out of true, the thing to keep is a self that does not panic and does not fester.

## The test

Take an organisation or a load you are part of. Ask where the ends are: what is weak at the root, what is weak at the tip, and what is packed in the middle. Then ask whether you are line 3 or line 4 — pushing against the beam, or letting the weight spread.
